newsitem.title: CHINA: HK-Taiwan set up high-level links after handover.
newsitem.headline: HK-Taiwan set up high-level links after handover.

text.p: Hong Kong, now a part of China, and Taiwan, branded a rebel province by Beijing, named two high-level intermediaries on Thursday to improve their cooperation, a senior Taiwan offical said.

Koo Chen-fu, Taipei's representative on Taiwan-China affairs, said he had opened the channel for dialogue with new Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa on the first working day after the former British colony's return to Chinese sovereignty.
Tung appointed a member of his inner advisory council, Paul Yip, to act as his intermediary in Taiwan-Hong Kong affairs, Koo told a news conference.
Koo, who had a half-hour meeting with Tung earlier, said Taipei hoped the channel could become more systematic and open in the future, acting as a bridge between the communities.
"The biggest issue now in front of us is how to increase cooperation on both sides, to pull closer the psychological rift created by history," he said.
Koo was in Hong Kong to attend the handover ceremonies marking the end of 156 years of British rule.
"Mr Tung specially said issues between the two places will be undertaken by Mr Paul Yip...and Cheng An-kuo," Koo said.
Cheng heads Taipei's unofficial mission in Hong Kong, the Chung Hwa Travel Agency.
"The two will talk and manage (Hong Kong-Taiwan affairs)," said Koo. "We hope this channel can be institutionalised."
There was some confusion on the status of the talks between Koo and Tung.
Beijing said no official contacts could take place between Taiwan and Hong Kong without its approval, and a Tung aide described the meeting as private.
A spokesman for Tung said Yip had been liaising with Taiwan for some time.

"The Chief Executive's adviser, Paul Yip, has been liaising informally for the past few weeks with Mr Cheng An-Kuo of the Chung Hwa Travel Service on matters relating to Hong Kong and Taiwan," he said. He declined to comment further.
Yip, a member of Tung's Executive Council, is a businessman known for his ability to maintain good ties with Taiwan and Beijing.
China has regarded Taiwan as a rebel province since the former Chinese Nationalist government lost the civil war to the communists in 1949 and took refuge on the island.
Beijing is working for the island's reunification with the mainland and considers the "one country, two systems" policy used in Hong Kong's return to China by Britain as a model.
Koo said Taipei hoped that its officials would be able to visit Hong Kong and vice versa, adding he had invited Tung to visit Taiwan but noted he knew the new leader was very busy.
